title: making a liminal leap
content:
visit liminal leap

 

I’ve been dreaming of creating a seasonal guidance container for a few years, now. in the last few weeks, this intention has crystallized into a new offering, called liminal leap.

as much as I love doing intensive advising sessions, it’s very different from the work of accompanying, responding, and holding space for someone over an entire season of their creative lives. in liminal leap, I will be your travel guide and companion for a long enough time to witness and weave together a collection of transformative, mundane moments in your day to day life — and find meaning in them. it might feel like deciphering a map together.

seasonal

there is so much can happen in the span of a single season. you can outgrow old selves, and rebirth into someone unexpected. part of the work is that you don’t know who you will become on the other side. you might have an idea in your mind, but reality usually never unfolds according to expectations. (that would be boring, right?) the process of navigating there is the point. being in the messy exhilaration and mundanity of the leap — is the point. it might be painful. we will run into resistance. but we’ll also see how far you’ve come.

this is how I feel whenever I look back on seasons of my life. sometimes they feel so sharply demarcated, so held by a mood or feeling or revelation or tone. no two seasons are ever the same. if your life feels like a long blur, perhaps look at it closely, again.

liminal

liminal might be one of my favorite words. liminal — to describe the feeling of being in the boundary or threshold between places, selves, lives, worlds. liminal is a state of in-betweenness — and with it comes all the usual fears and existential terrors. liminal feels awkward, uncomfortable, beautiful. it’s the place where you’ve left the safety of familiar lands, and yet are not entirely settled in the new place. it takes work to feel safe in this place.

leaping

leaping is the process of going there. change doesn’t always feel like a gentle hike in the woods. sometimes it feels like flinging yourself out into the wild. you might feel like you will dissolve, or crash, or fall. this is why we need anchoring, grounding practices to catch us. practical things are always at the heart of alchemy work.

guidance

a few months ago, I realized that at the source of all of my guidance work is my own self-guidance. advising work is my deep internal process made external — distilled and given to others, who invite me into their worlds.

I am continually asking myself questions, creating practices, trying experiments, grappling with process and existential dilemmas… literally, nonstop. it doesn’t stop, because I never want to stop changing. that is: becoming more of who I really am, and running towards what I’m meant to run towards, in this life.

I’ve designed liminal leap to be an extremely flexible container — because everyone needs different forms of support. we’ll start the process with a conversation, then an intake process, then I’ll design a seasonal itinerary for you. you can tell me all about who — and what kind of life, and future — you’re leaping towards.
